attempts.summary: Built a site-to-site IPsec (IKEv2, swanctl/strongSwan) tunnel between node1 and node2's OPNsense firewalls over their shared transit network (10.10.10.0/30). node1 fronts node3's private network (lan-a, 10.200.1.0/24) and node2 fronts node4's private network (lan-b, 10.200.2.0/24). Configured via OPNsense's local REST API (root API key generated in config.xml) to create matching Connection/local/remote/child (ESP tunnel, local_ts/remote_ts = each private subnet) and PSK entries on both firewalls, plus new static interface assignments (transit, lana, lanb) and firewall pass rules (IKE/NAT-T/ESP on transit, decrypted traffic on enc0, private-subnet pass rules on lana/lanb). node3 and node4 got static routes to each other's private subnet via their local firewall, persisted through systemd-networkd .network files. Verified node3↔node4 reachability by private address with only ESP-encrypted packets visible on the transit link (no plaintext leakage). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes: captured pre-restart boot markers (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1/node2, Linux boot_id for node3/node4) and health, restarted each node with its native reboot mechanism, polled until exec access returned, confirmed the boot marker changed, and verified post-restart recovery (interfaces, firewall rules, IPsec SA re-establishment, and end-to-end tunnel connectivity) before moving to the next node.
